card.title: The team loop enforces a role's max_context: a nudge at 75%, then stop or trim
card.description:
A role's max_context (RoleSpec, airlie.yaml: the coder's is 65536) is read by the doctor and by task serve, and by nothing in the team loop: NativeTeam stops a run only at ctx.token_budget (200,000: the largest prompt plus everything generated) or max_steps. AIR-7's layer 01 run on 2026-10-18 (20261018-155119-0cfb) reached 80,670 prompt tokens at step 26, well past the role's limit, because five reads of one capped file added ~25k tokens; the engine accepted it (the studio profile's max_kv_size is 131072), every later step was a long-context decode (15-20 s for a 90-token reply), and nothing said the role was over its context.

Scope: the team loop knows the role's max_context and acts before the prompt passes it.
- A `context` event when a step's prompt_tokens first pass 75% of max_context (team_id, role, step, prompt_tokens, max_context), so the job screen and the metrics page can show it, and the role is told once: "Your context is at N of M tokens. Stop reading: write from what you have." (the same shape as the write-now nudges in native_team.py).
- At max_context itself, one of two things, chosen in config (RoleSpec.on_context_full: "stop" | "trim", default "stop"): stop the run with stop_reason "context_full" and a final text that says so (the layer then blocks with a reason a person can act on, instead of grinding to max_steps); or trim: drop the oldest tool observations (not the assistant's own messages or the goal) by replacing their content with "[observation dropped: N chars from read_file src/x.py]" until the prompt fits, and emit `context_trimmed` (team_id, role, step, dropped, chars). Trimming changes the prompt's prefix, so the next turn is a cold prefill: the event says so and AIR-27's cached_tokens shows the cost.
- The decision uses the prompt_tokens the engine reported for the last request (GenResult.prompt_tokens), not an estimate.
- Not in scope: summarising dropped observations with a model; changing the output cap (read_file's range, from the read_file PR, is the fix for a file that does not fit).

Done when
- A FakeEngine run whose reported prompt_tokens cross 75% of max_context gets the one nudge and the `context` event; one that reaches max_context stops with "context_full" (default) or, with on_context_full: trim, continues with the oldest observations replaced and `context_trimmed` emitted; a run under the limit is unchanged.
- The job screen shows the context line for a running subtask (with AIR-29's live line if it is in, else as an event in the list).
- task check passes.

story.title: Enforce a role's max_context in the team loop
story.summary: A specialist role (e.g. the coder, max_context 65536) can be pushed past its own context limit by a few large reads, after which every later step is a slow long-context decode and nothing tells the role or the operator it is over. The team loop should know the role's max_context, nudge the role once at 75%, and at the limit either stop with a reason a person can act on or trim the oldest observations, so a run is bounded by the role's context rather than the engine's.

acceptance.given: a FakeEngine run whose role has max_context 65536 (on_context_full left at its default) and whose reported GenResult.prompt_tokens first cross 75% of max_context (49152) on some step
acceptance.when: the loop processes that step and then makes the next generation request
acceptance.then: exactly one user message is appended to the conversation before the next request, with the text 'Your context is at {prompt_tokens} of {max_context} tokens. Stop reading: write from what you have.' (both numbers the engine's reported values), and ctx.emit is called once with kind 'context' and fields team_id, role, step, prompt_tokens, max_context; a second crossing in the same run emits no further nudge and no further 'context' event

acceptance.given: a FakeEngine run whose role has on_context_full 'stop' (the default) and whose reported prompt_tokens reach or exceed max_context
acceptance.then: the run stops with stop_reason 'context_full' and final_text 'stopped: context full at {max_context} tokens', and no further generation request is made for that role

acceptance.given: a FakeEngine run whose role has on_context_full 'trim' and whose reported prompt_tokens reach or exceed max_context, with at least one tool observation in the conversation
acceptance.when: the loop trims the oldest tool observations (role 'tool' messages only, never the goal, the assistant's own messages, or the system prompt) by replacing each dropped observation's content with '[observation dropped: {chars} chars from {tool_name}]' until the prompt fits, where {chars} is that observation's original content length and {tool_name} its tool name
acceptance.then: the run continues (does not stop), the next generation request is sent with the trimmed messages, and ctx.emit is called with kind 'context_trimmed' and fields team_id, role, step, dropped (count of observations replaced) and chars (total characters removed)

acceptance.given: a FakeEngine run whose reported prompt_tokens never reach 75% of the role's max_context
acceptance.when: the run completes as it does today
acceptance.then: no 'context' or 'context_trimmed' event is emitted, no context nudge message is appended, the stop_reason is whatever it was before this change, and the conversation messages are byte-for-byte identical to a run without this feature

acceptance.given: a role whose on_context_full is set to a value other than 'stop' or 'trim' (e.g. 'pause')
acceptance.then: loading fails with an error that names the key path and quotes the allowed values, e.g. 'roles.<name>.on_context_full must be one of: stop, trim'

acceptance.given: the job screen viewing a running studio subtask whose role has emitted a 'context' event
acceptance.when: the subtask's detail panel is drawn
acceptance.then: it shows a context line reading 'Context: {prompt_tokens} / {max_context} tokens' (the values from the event) in the subtask's facts, and the 'context' event also appears in the Events timeline with its fields

out_of_scope: Summarising dropped observations with a model (trim replaces them with a fixed placeholder only)
Changing read_file's output cap / range (the fix for a single file that does not fit; that is the read_file PR)
Any change to the engine's max_kv_size or the team-level token_budget stop
The metrics page rendering (only the job screen is in scope per the request; the 'context'/'context_trimmed' events carry the fields a metrics page would need)
assumptions: The 75% nudge and the limit decision both key off the engine-reported GenResult.prompt_tokens for the last request, not an estimate, per the request
on_context_full is a new field on RoleSpec (schema.py) defaulting to 'stop', so existing airlie.yaml files are unchanged
'oldest tool observations' means the earliest role='tool' messages in conversation order; the goal, system, and assistant messages are never trimmed
The nudge text and the 'context'/'context_trimmed' event field names are exactly as specified in the request, so the job screen and any metrics page can rely on them
The job screen's existing digest()/drawDetail() is extended to read the 'context' event; AIR-29's live line is not assumed to be present, so the line falls back to the event in the list

survey:
Survey notes for the engineer who will plan the layers.

## 1. Files and symbols the change touches or must follow

**The team loop — `src/airlie/teams/native_team.py`**
- `NativeTeam.run` (line 258) is the only place the loop enforces context today: it stops at `ctx.token_budget` (line 527–532) and `ctx.max_steps` (line 574–579). It never reads `ctx.role.max_context`. The new enforcement goes here.
- The decision must use `res.prompt_tokens` (line 350–351: `prompt_tokens += res.prompt_tokens; max_prompt = max(max_prompt, res.prompt_tokens)`). `res` is a `GenResult` from `self.engine.generate(req)` (line 344). `max_prompt` is the high-water mark of the *last* request's reported prompt tokens — that is the value to compare against `ctx.role.max_context`.
- The existing nudge pattern to copy: `WRITE_NOW` (line 104), `WRITE_ONLY` (line 110), `ACT_FIRST` (line 159), `STILL_RED` (line 168) — each is a module-level constant with a docstring, appended as `Message(role="user", content=...)` and guarded by a one-shot `*_warned` bool. The new "stop reading" nudge at 75% should follow this exact shape (a constant + a `context_warned` bool + `ctx.emit("context", ...)`).
- `ctx.emit` is the event sink (see `TeamContext.emit`, protocol.py line 92). Existing emits in this file: `malformed_call` (line 241), `text_before_action` (line 384), `read_refused` (line 449), `write_deadline` (line 537). New events `context` and `context_trimmed` go through the same `ctx.emit`.
- `StopReason` is a `Literal` in `src/airlie/teams/protocol.py` line 18–29. Adding `"context_full"` means adding it there.
- Trimming operates on the `messages: list[Message]` list (line 263). Tool observations are `Message(role="tool", ...)` (line 461–463); the goal is the first user message; the system prompt is `Message(role="system", ...)` (line 275). Trim = replace the `content` of the oldest `role=="tool"` messages with `"[observation dropped: N chars from read_file src/x.py]"` (the tool name is in `Message.name`, line 462). Do not touch `role=="assistant"` or the goal `role=="user"` message.

**The config — `src/airlie/config/schema.py`**
- `RoleSpec` (line 135) has `max_context: int = 65536` (line 140). The new field `on_context_full: Literal["stop", "trim"] = "stop"` goes here, next to the other per-role behaviour flags (`nudge_stuck` line 155, `green_before_done` line 161, `write_schedule` line 166).
- `RoleSpec` is a `Strict` pydantic model — a new field with a default is backward-compatible, but the config tests (below) enumerate fields.

**The engine result — `src/airlie/engine/types.py`**
- `GenResult.prompt_tokens` is the reported value the decision uses. (I did not read this file; the loop already consumes `res.prompt_tokens` at native_team.py:350, so the field exists. Confirm the exact type before writing the comparison.)

**The job screen — `src/airlie/serve/web/screens/job.js`**
- The "Done when" requires the job screen to show the context line for a running subtask. This screen renders events; the new `context` / `context_trimmed` events must be rendered there (and the metrics page per the request). I did not read this file — the planner must, to see how existing events (e.g. `write_deadline`, `read_refused`) are surfaced and whether there is a "live line" (AIR-29) to attach to.

**Where max_context is read today (must not be broken)**
- `src/airlie/doctor.py` and `src/airlie/serve/` (task serve) read `max_context` per the request. The team loop is the third reader. The change is additive; those readers are untouched.

## 2. Where the tests live and how they are named

- **Team loop:** `tests/unit/test_native_team.py` (59 KB — the big one). It uses a `FakeEngine` (from `src/airlie/engine/fake.py`, tested in `tests/unit/test_fake_engine.py`). The "Done when" criteria (FakeEngine crossing 75% → one nudge + `context` event; reaching max_context → `context_full` stop or trim + `context_trimmed`; under limit → unchanged) all belong here. Tests are named `test_*` and drive `NativeTeam.run(ctx, observer)` with a `TeamContext` whose `role` is a `RoleSpec` and whose `emit` captures events.
- **Config schema:** `tests/unit/test_config.py` (40 KB) and `tests/unit/test_config_messages.py`. A new `RoleSpec` field needs a test that it parses from YAML and that the default is `"stop"`.
- **StopReason / protocol:** covered indirectly by `test_native_team.py`; if `StopReason` is asserted as a set anywhere, that assertion must include `"context_full"`.
- **Job screen:** `tests/unit/test_serve_web.py` (3 KB, small) and `tests/unit/test_serve.py` / `test_serve_jobs.py`. The web-screen test is the one to extend for the context line.

## 3. Conventions and registries a new name must be added to

- **`StopReason` Literal** (`protocol.py:18`): add `"context_full"`. This is a closed `Literal`, so any consumer that matches on stop reasons (the studio pipeline, the job screen's status rendering, `docs`/metrics) will need to know it. Grep for `"token_budget"` and `"max_steps"` to find every place stop reasons are branched on — those are the registries to extend.
- **Event kinds:** there is no central registry of event `kind` strings — `EventSink.emit(kind, **fields)` (events.py:17) is free-form, and `ctx.emit` is `Callable[..., None]`. So `context` and `context_trimmed` need no registration, *but* the job screen and metrics page must be told to render them (they almost certainly have a kind→renderer map or a list of known kinds). That list is the de-facto registry.
- **`RoleSpec` field** (`schema.py:135`): `on_context_full` is a new `Strict`-model field. `Strict` means unknown fields are rejected, so adding a defaulted field is safe for existing YAML, but `airlie.yaml` (lines 99–146) and `airlie.local.example.yaml` may want it set explicitly, and `test_config.py` likely asserts the full field set or a round-trip.
- **`airlie.yaml`**: the coder's `max_context: 65536` (line 99) is the value the 75%/100% thresholds key off. No YAML change is strictly required (default `"stop"`), but if the team wants trim for the coder, that is a YAML edit.

## 4. Things that could make a test pass for the wrong reason before the change

- **The 75% nudge test can pass on the base by accident** if the FakeEngine's reported `prompt_tokens` happen to also trip the existing `token_budget` check (line 527) or `max_steps` (line 574) at the same step. The test must assert the *specific* new behaviour: exactly one `context` event with `prompt_tokens`/`max_context` fields, and that the run *continues* past 75% (does not stop). A test that only asserts "the run stopped" would be satisfied by the pre-existing `token_budget`/`max_steps` stops. The brief must require asserting the `context` event's presence and the run's continuation, not just a stop.
- **The `context_full` stop test** must set `token_budget` high enough (or the role's `max_context` low enough) that `max_context` is hit *before* `token_budget` and `max_steps`, so the stop is genuinely `context_full` and not the pre-existing `token_budget`/`max_steps`. Otherwise it passes for the wrong reason.
- **The trim test** must assert the `context_trimmed` event *and* that the next request's prompt actually shrank (the FakeEngine should report a lower `prompt_tokens` on the following turn, or the test inspects the trimmed `messages`). A test that only asserts the event fired, without confirming the oldest tool observation's content was replaced, would not prove trimming works.
- **The "under the limit is unchanged" test** is the guard against over-eager enforcement: it must assert no `context`/`context_trimmed` event and no `context_full` stop when `prompt_tokens` stays below 75%. This one is safe on the base (nothing emits these events yet), so it is a good first layer.
- **`max_prompt` vs per-step `prompt_tokens`:** the loop tracks `max_prompt` (line 351) as a running max. The 75% nudge should fire when a step's `prompt_tokens` *first* passes 75% — using `res.prompt_tokens` for that step, and a one-shot flag so it fires once. If the planner instead compares the cumulative `prompt_tokens` (line 350, which *sums* across steps) against `max_context`, the test would pass for the wrong reason (the sum crosses 75% far earlier than any single prompt does). The request explicitly says "the prompt_tokens the engine reported for the last request" — that is the per-step `res.prompt_tokens`, not the running sum.

## Key open questions for the planner

1. **Trim mechanics:** the request says drop oldest tool observations until the prompt fits. The loop only knows `res.prompt_tokens` (a count), not a per-message token breakdown, so "until the prompt fits" cannot be computed exactly from tokens alone. The planner must decide the trim trigger (e.g. "at max_context, drop oldest N observations" or "drop until estimated prompt < max_context" using a char→token heuristic) and whether the trim is re-measured on the next `res.prompt_tokens`. This is the one genuine design decision the request leaves open.
2. **Job screen "live line" (AIR-29):** the request says show the context line "with AIR-29's live line if it is in, else as an event in the list." The planner must check whether AIR-29's live line exists in `job.js` to know which branch to take.
3. **`GenResult.prompt_tokens` type/semantics** in `engine/types.py` — confirm it is the per-request prompt token count (it is consumed as such at native_team.py:350, but the planner should read the dataclass to be sure of the field name and that it is the *input* tokens, not total).

layers.title: RoleSpec.on_context_full and StopReason 'context_full'
layers.brief: Add `on_context_full` to RoleSpec (schema.py, next to nudge_stuck/green_before_done) defaulting to 'stop', allowed values 'stop' and 'trim', with a validator that rejects any other value with an error naming the key path and quoting the allowed values, e.g. 'roles.<name>.on_context_full must be one of: stop, trim' (put the check where the role name is known — the config-level roles dict — and read the rest of schema.py to place it; the test must see the substring 'on_context_full must be one of: stop, trim'). Add 'context_full' to the StopReason Literal in protocol.py. Tests in test_config.py: a role YAML with on_context_full: pause fails to load with that message; a role without it parses with default 'stop'; existing airlie.yaml still loads. Fails before (field absent / pydantic default message), passes after. Do not touch the loop or the job screen here.

layers.title: Team loop: 75% nudge and stop at the role's max_context
layers.brief: In NativeTeam.run, after a step is fully processed (tool observation appended), compare the last request's reported res.prompt_tokens against ctx.role.max_context. At 75% or more (>= 0.75 * max_context), once per run (a context_warned bool, following the WRITE_NOW/STILL_RED idiom: module-level constant + one-shot bool + ctx.emit), append exactly one user message 'Your context is at {prompt_tokens} of {max_context} tokens. Stop reading: write from what you have.' (both numbers the engine's reported values) and emit kind 'context' with fields team_id, role, step, prompt_tokens, max_context; a second crossing emits nothing more. At max_context or more with on_context_full 'stop' (the default), break with stop_reason 'context_full' and final_text 'stopped: context full at {max_context} tokens' — no further generation request. Tests in test_native_team.py using FakeEngine (its prompt_tokens is the request's word count, so use a small max_context or a large observation to cross the thresholds): (AC1) first crossing 75% appends exactly one such user message before the next request, one 'context' emit with those five fields, no second nudge on a later crossing; (AC2) reaching max_context stops with 'context_full' and that final_text, and the engine sees no further request for the role; (AC4) a run that never reaches 75% emits no 'context'/'context_trimmed' events, appends no nudge, keeps its old stop_reason, and the messages of every request are byte-for-byte identical to a run without the feature. Prove AC4's no-op by asserting zero new user messages and zero new events, not just the stop_reason.

layers.title: Team loop: trim oldest tool observations at the limit
layers.brief: Extend the same check site: when the last request's reported prompt_tokens reaches or exceeds ctx.role.max_context and ctx.role.on_context_full is 'trim', replace the content of the oldest role=='tool' messages (conversation order; never the goal, system, or assistant messages) with '[observation dropped: {chars} chars from {tool_name}]' ({chars} = that observation's original content length, {tool_name} = Message.name), dropping oldest-first until the conversation's estimated prompt (sum of message content chars / 4) fits under max_context; then continue the run (do not stop) and emit kind 'context_trimmed' with fields team_id, role, step, dropped (count replaced) and chars (total characters removed). Test in test_native_team.py: a role with on_context_full 'trim' and a large tool observation that pushes the reported prompt_tokens past max_context — assert the run continues, the next request's messages contain the placeholder text with the original char count and tool name, the goal/system/assistant messages are untouched, and the 'context_trimmed' emit carries dropped and chars. Fails before (no trim branch: the run stops with 'context_full' instead), passes after.

layers.title: Job screen: context line in the subtask facts
layers.scope: src/airlie/serve/web/screens/job.js, tests/unit/test_serve_web.py, and the studio pipeline file that wires TeamContext.emit to the job event log (locate it by grepping for emit= in src/airlie/serve)
layers.brief: In job.js digest(), add a case for kind 'context' that records the latest {prompt_tokens, max_context} on the subtask node (keyed by e.team_id, which is the subtask id); in drawDetail()'s facts dl, render a row 'Context: {prompt_tokens} / {max_context} tokens' from it (fall back to the event in the list per the story's assumption — no AIR-29 live line). The Events timeline needs no kind-specific change: summarize() already prints every non-skipped field, so a 'context' event appears with its fields — say so in the test. First verify the studio forwards arbitrary event kinds from ctx.emit into the job's event log; if kinds are filtered anywhere, add 'context' and 'context_trimmed' there. Test in test_serve_web.py: feed digest() a 'context' event for a running subtask and assert the node carries the values and the drawn detail contains the exact line; feed the same event list to the timeline path and assert the event renders with its fields. Fails before (no 'context' case in digest: the facts row is absent), passes after.
